Consumer sentiment fell 8% in August compared to last month, according to preliminary data from the University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers. Released Friday, the latest sentiment reading ended two consecutive months of improvement as Americans feel the effects of the Iran war pushing up fuel, energy and food prices.
results.title: Consumer sentiment and retail spending are down

results.content:
Consumer sentiment fell about 8% this August, ending two consecutive months of improvement. While views of personal finances saw only minor declines, expected business conditions sank 11% for the short run and 17% for the long run. Decreases in sentiment were seen across the political spectrum, with Republicans exhibiting the strongest month-to-month decline in August. Sentiment among Republicans is now 19% below readings just prior to the Iran conflict and the lowest since the 2024 election. [...] August 15, 2026 – On Friday, the University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Preliminary Results for August was released.  
  
Note: August 2024 Consumer Sentiment under President Biden was 67.9
results.title: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Preliminary Results for August 2026 Declines 8% Month-Over-Month, Year-ahead Inflation Expectations Rise to 4.3%. Sentiment Under Trump is Down 12.4% Year-Over-Year and 25% Lower Than Biden in August
